Here $N_{a} = 10$

and $N_{b} = 10$

In O atom 8 electrons present, so in $O_{2},  8$ $\times$ 2 = 16 electrons present. 

Then in $O_{2}^{+}$ no of electrons = 15 

in $O_{2}^{-}$  no of electrons = 17

in $O_{2}^{2-}$ no of electrons = 18

$\therefore \quad$ Molecular orbital configuration of $O_{2} (16$ electrons) is 

$σ_{1s^{2}}σ_{1s^{2}}^{\ast }$ $σ_{2s^{2}}σ_{2s^{2}}^{\ast }$ $σ_{2p_{z}^{2}}π_{2p_{x}^{2}}=π_{2p_{y}^{2}}π_{2p_{x}^{1}}^{\ast }=π_{2p_{y}^{1}}^{\ast }$

$\therefore \quadN_{a} = 6$

$N_{b} = 10$

$\therefore \quad$ BO = $\frac{1}{2}[10-6]=2$

Molecular orbital configuration of O${}_{2}^{+}$ (15 electrons) is 

$σ_{1s^{2}}σ_{1s^{2}}^{\ast }σ_{2s^{2}}σ_{2s^{2}}^{\ast }σ_{2p_{z}^{2}}π_{2p_{x}^{2}}=π_{2p_{y}^{2}}π_{2p_{x}^{1}}^{\ast }=π_{2p_{y}^{o}}^{\ast }$

$\therefore \quad$ $N_{b} = 10$

$N_{a} = 5$ 

$\therefore \quad$  BO = $\frac{1}{2}[10-5]$ = 2.5

Molecular orbital configuration of $O_{2}^{-}$ (17 electrons) is 

$σ_{1s^{2}}σ_{1s^{2}}^{\ast }σ_{2s^{2}}σ_{2s^{2}}^{\ast }σ_{2p_{z}^{2}}π_{2p_{x}^{2}}=π_{2p_{y}^{2}}π_{2p_{x}^{2}}^{\ast }=π_{2p_{y}^{1}}^{\ast }$

$\therefore \quad$ $N_{b} = 10$

$N_{a} = 7$

$\therefore \quad$ BO = $\frac{1}{2}[10-7]$ = 1.5

Molecular orbital configuration of O ${}_{2}^{2-}$ (18 electrons) is

$\therefore \quad$ $N_{b} = 10$

$N_{a} = 8$

$\therefore \quad$ BO = $\frac{1}{2}$ [ 10 $-$ 8] = 1

As Bond strength $\propto$ Bond order so,  correct order is 

$O_{2}^{2-}<O_{2}^{-}<O_{2}<O_{2}^{+}$

text: Identify the species having one $π$-bond and maximum number of canonical forms from the following :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{SO}{}_{3}$: sulphur forms three $\mathrm{S}=\mathrm{O}$ double bonds (one $pπ$–$pπ$ and two $pπ$–$dπ$), so it has three $π$-bonds.

$\mathrm{SO}{}_{2}$: sulphur forms two $\mathrm{S}=\mathrm{O}$ double bonds, so it has two $π$-bonds.

$\mathrm{O}{}_{2}$: the $\mathrm{O}=\mathrm{O}$ bond has one $π$-bond, but the molecule has only one Lewis structure.

$\mathrm{CO}{}_{3}{}^{2-}$: there is one $\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{O}$ double bond and two $\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{O}{}^{-}$ single bonds, so there is one $π$-bond; the double bond can be placed at any of the three oxygen atoms, giving three canonical forms.


[IMG]

Hence, the correct option is (D).

text: Which among the following is the strongest acid ?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Acid strength depends on the stability of the conjugate base formed when a C–H proton is lost.

(A) Butane gives a localised alkyl carbanion, so it is an extremely weak acid ($\mathrm{p}K_{a}\approx 50$).

(B) Toluene gives the benzyl anion, delocalised into the ring by resonance, so it is more acidic than butane ($\mathrm{p}K_{a}\approx 41$).

(C) Cyclopropene loses H from its $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}$ to give the cyclopropenyl anion, a planar cyclic conjugated system with $4π$ electrons; it is antiaromatic and very unstable, so cyclopropene is a very weak acid.

(D) Cyclopentadiene loses H from its $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}$ to give the cyclopentadienyl anion, a planar cyclic conjugated system with $6π$ electrons that obeys Hückel's $(4n+2)$ rule; it is aromatic and strongly stabilised ($\mathrm{p}K_{a}\approx 16$).


[IMG]

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift

text:
An accelerated electron has a speed of 5 $\times$ $10^{6} ms^{-1}$ with an uncertainty of 0.02%. The uncertainty in finding its location while in motion is x $\times$ $10^{-9} m$. The value of x is $____________. ($Nearest integer)

[Use mass of electron = 9.1 $\times$ $10^{-31} kg, h =6.63$ $\times$ $10^{-34} Js$, $π$ = 3.14]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\Delta v=\frac{0.02}{100}\times 5\times 10^{6}=10^{3}$ m/s

$\Delta x.\Delta v=\frac{h}{4πm}$

$\Rightarrow$ $x\times 10^{-9}\times 10^{3}=\frac{6.63\times 10^{-34}}{4\times 3.14\times 9.1\times 10^{-31}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $x\times 10^{-9}\times 10^{3}=0.058\times 10^{-3}$

$\Rightarrow$ $x=\frac{0.058\times 10^{-6}}{10^{-9}}=58$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift

text: For a chemical reaction A $\to$ B, it was found that concentration of B is increased by 0.2 mol $L^{-}$ in 30 min. The average rate of the reaction is $____________$ $\times$ $10^{-1}$ mol $L^{-1} h^{-1}. ($in nearest integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For the reaction

$\mathrm{A}\to \mathrm{B}$

the average rate in terms of formation of $\mathrm{B}$ is

$\text{Average rate}=\frac{\Delta [\mathrm{B}]}{\Delta t}$

Given,

$\Delta [\mathrm{B}]=0.2\mathrm{mol}\mathrm{L}^{-1}$

and

$\Delta t=30\min =0.5\mathrm{h}$

Thus,

$\text{Average rate}=\frac{0.2}{0.5}=0.4\mathrm{mol}\mathrm{L}^{-1}\mathrm{h}^{-1}$

$0.4=4\times 10^{-1}$

Hence, the nearest integer is

$4$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift
